candidates.title: Selection-Based Structured Reasoning: Toward Efficient Multimodal Search Agents
candidates.summary: Multimodal agents commonly generate freeform reasoning before each action. To address this challenge, we introduce Selection-based Structured Reasoning (SSR), a framework that reformulates reasoning as selection instead of open-ended generation. candidates.title: Plan or Retrieve First? A Scale Study of Tool Discovery Architectures
candidates.summary: Tool-augmented LLM agents discover relevant APIs from large registries before planning execution, yet finite context windows prohibit injecting all tool definitions into a single prompt. The dominant approach, which we term Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP), embeds the user query and retrieves similar tools via approximate nearest-neighbor search. We study an alternative Plan-then-Retrieve (PtR) paradigm in which the LLM first generates Abstract Tool Stubs (hypothesized function signatures describing needed capabilities) which then serve as retrieval queries against the registry. candidates.title: Smallwords: controlled-vocabulary generation with one inspectable contract
candidates.summary:
I built smallwords, a small MIT-licensed Python package for controlled-vocabulary LLM output.

The practical problem is drift. A project may describe its allowed language in a prompt, encode it again in a grammar, approximate it in JSON Schema, and then write separate validation logic. smallwords keeps one WordlistSpec at the center and derives all four surfaces from it:

  • prompt guidance
  • GBNF for constrained decoding
  • JSON Schema
  • post-generation validation

candidates.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
candidates.summary: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. candidates.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
candidates.summary: We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder.
